findings.claim: The `boilerplate_stripped` sub-assertion labelled "the reconstruction identity" cannot fail - it only tests that the first span's slice is non-blank, which `find_chrome` guarantees by construction, so the R2 acceptance clause "normalized_text[start:end] still reconstructs the original run" is claimed but not actually asserted.
findings.evidence: src/sec10k/eval_adapter.py:281-282 `if not text[b["start"]:b["end"]].strip(): return "chrome run does not reconstruct to its original text"`. `text` is `result["normalized_text"]` and is never passed through `strip_chrome`, so the branch is independent of the function under test; and every kind in `find_chrome` requires a non-blank stripped line, so no span the envelope can publish makes the slice blank. Monkeypatched `strip_chrome` with 7 wrong implementations (total no-op, +1 shift, remove-head-N, remove-tail-N, spans-treated-as-window-relative, start/end ignored, end-1 off-by-one) against msft-2013 and jpm-2024: all 7 went red, none of them via this branch. `tasks/reviews/pr25-r1-resolution.json` R2 fix item (d) states it verifies that "normalized_text[start:end] still returns its original characters" - it does not.
findings.repro: Check every published span reconstructs non-blank on msft-2013 -> True for all; and grep the branch: no `strip_chrome` result is compared against an expected string anywhere in the check.
findings.acceptance: Either the branch compares the reconstructed slice against something the case declares (as `boilerplate._demo`:173 does with a literal), or it is deleted and the resolution/ADR stop crediting `boilerplate_stripped` with a reconstruction assertion. The other four sub-assertions already carry R2 and should stay.

findings.claim: The resolution artifact's residual-risk statement that `boilerplate-section-heads` "does not pin [MIN_SPREAD] from above" and that "no case asserts a running head that a HIGHER spread gate would drop" is false - the case is pinned from above and goes red at MIN_SPREAD = 0.83.
findings.evidence: tasks/reviews/pr25-r1-resolution.json, `unverified[2]`. jpm-2024's real running head `JPMorgan Chase & Co./2024 Form 10-K` has measured spread 0.8202 (286 occurrences, CV 0.368), and evals/adversarial/boilerplate-section-heads.json asserts `{"kind":"running_head","min":280}` plus `{"kind":"page_number","min":280}`. Raising MIN_SPREAD past 0.8202 drops jpm-2024 from 572 spans to 0, so the case is red. Measured sweep: MIN_SPREAD 0.65-0.82 changes nothing on any of the 37 fixtures; 0.83, 0.90, 0.95 all take jpm-2024 to 0 spans; 0.50/0.60 take it to 580 and 0.40 to 653.
findings.repro: Set MIN_SPREAD = 0.83 and run `python3 -m evals.run --suite fast --no-report` -> [FAIL] boilerplate-section-heads, 74/75 = 0.987. ORCHESTRATOR RE-RAN THIS INDEPENDENTLY: reproduces exactly.
findings.acceptance: The `unverified` bullet is corrected to state that MIN_SPREAD is now pinned on both sides (red at 0.40 and at 0.83, green in 0.65-0.82), leaving only the MIN_REPEATS half - which the reviewer re-ran and which is accurate: MIN_REPEATS 8->20 leaves fast at 75/75 with only `_demo` red.

findings.claim: `boilerplate-section-heads`' provenance (and the matching resolution text) states the wrong mechanism for R5: it says jpm-2024 "puts its page number ABOVE the running head" and therefore exercises the `neighbour(i, -1)` branch, but jpm-2024 splits exactly 143/143 between the two directions, and a number placed above its head is found by the *below* branch, not the above one.
findings.evidence: evals/adversarial/boilerplate-section-heads.json provenance, R5 paragraph; tasks/reviews/pr25-r1-resolution.json R5 `fix`. Measured on jpm-2024 normalized_text: of the 286 detected `page_number` lines, 143 have their chrome neighbour ABOVE only (line index 2590, text `49`, preceded by `JPMorgan Chase & Co./2024 Form 10-K`) and 143 have it BELOW only (line index 2722, text `50`, followed by the same head). Consequently both single-direction mutations give 143, not just the below-only one - the coverage is better than the provenance claims, but the stated fixture property is not what the fixture does.
findings.repro: Both single-direction mutations of the adjacency condition give jpm-2024 143 page numbers and both turn the case red (fast 74/75). ORCHESTRATOR RE-RAN THIS INDEPENDENTLY: above-only -> 143, below-only -> 143.
findings.acceptance: The provenance says jpm-2024 alternates (143 numbers above their head, 143 below) and that the case therefore pins BOTH halves of the adjacency rule - which is what it actually does - instead of naming one direction.
